title: Handoff signal: sprint crash course — 2027-06-02
content:
Overview
This is a lightweight, practical handoff + weekly operational notes doc for the SRE rotation covering 2027-05-27 -> 2027-06-02. Goal: reduce cross-shift context friction by introducing a ‘signal card’ (shortest actionable summary) and a small set of mitigations we can try next sprint. Use this during handoffs and pair-review the card in the first 10 minutes of the shift.

Quick summary (TL;DR)
- Incidents: 2 user-impact incidents (both transient latency spikes due to autoscaler and a cache-thrashing pattern), 3 non-user-facing degradations (queue backlog, metric aggregation lag, exporter crashloop).
- SLO: embeddings-p99 at 420ms (target 350ms) — on-call mitigations kept user error budget within 0.8% for the week.
- Actionables for next sprint: tighten autoscaler cooldowns for the generation workers; add a KV-cache eviction-warning metric and a temporary circuit-breaker; reduce noisy alerting threshold for exporter restarts.

Incident notes (concise)
1) Incident: autoscaler overshoot -> 2027-06-01 02:14 UTC
   - Symptom: sudden p95/p99 latency spike on hosted inference; surge of queued requests that timed out at the load balancer.
   - Root cause (first-pass): spike was correlated with a short-lived traffic pattern from a single org running batched eval jobs. Autoscaler scale-up took 6s but scale-down started pre-maturely when one AZ reported lower utilization, causing imbalance and head-of-line blocking.
   - Mitigation applied: temporarily pinned worker pools for affected customer to dedicated burst pool; bumped target concurrency for generation pods; rolled back recent scale-down tuning (PR linked).
   - Postmortem action items: add zone-aware autoscaler decision logging; add synthetic canary traffic test for bursty batched requests; adjust coordinator to prefer scale-up stability if a single org accounts for >40% of active requests.

2) Incident: KV cache thrash leading to regen penalty -> 2027-05-29 11:03 UTC
   - Symptom: model token generation latencies increased across sessions after a series of LLM prompting patterns that cause frequent KV invalidations (very long-tail prefixes). Cache hit dropped from 87% -> 31%.
   - First-pass RCA: recent prompt templating change in example app increased prefix diversity; combined with small cache-window config (30s) caused heavy eviction.
   - Short-term mitigation: increased per-session cache TTL to 90s for the affected model family; enabled temporary backend-side prefix dedupe for near-duplicate prefixes.
   - Longer-term: add eviction-warning metric (see action item below), and implement a smarter LRU + frequency hybrid for KV caches.

Non-user degradations
- Metrics exporter restarted repeatedly (kube probe flapping) — change: lowered liveness probe sensitivity and added jitter to scheduled export.
- Aggregation job latency increased; discovered that time-window partitioning job had a skew due to daylight-savings edge-case; fixed partition logic and backfilled missing partitions.
- Queue backlog (internal batch queue): observed slow consumers due to a GC pause on JVM worker; scheduled heap tuning and GC ergonomics change for the next deployment.

SLO status and reasoning
- embeddings-p99: 420ms (target 350) — main contributor was KV cache drop and autoscaler imbalance during bursts.
- generation-error-rate: 0.23% (target 0.5%) — fine.
- availability (99.95 target): stayed within target; the incidents were transient and mitigations avoided SLA violations.

Handoff Signal Card (new template)
- Short title: <one-line summary> e.g., "Autoscaler imbalance during org-batched evals"
- Impact: <user-facing impact> e.g., "p99 embeddings increased 70ms for ~30m; some LB timeouts"
- Status: <open|mitigated|monitoring> e.g., "mitigated (temporary pin)"
- Immediate next step (assigned): <who> + <what> e.g., "@Carlos: add zone-aware autoscaler logs; PR: infra#4821"
- Follow-up deadline: <date> e.g., "2027-06-09"
- Notes: free text short guidance (e.g., run load test id: canary/burst-0627)

Why this card? Keep handoffs empathetic to time-limited responders. The card must be readable in <90s. We want the oncoming oncall to have everything to make a quick decision (re-run canary, rollback change, escalate).

Operational experiments to run next sprint (small, targeted)
- Autoscaler: reduce scale-down aggressiveness and add a 20s cooldown for AZ-level decisions; run canary traffic that simulates single-customer batched workloads.
- KV-cache: emit eviction-rate and eviction-reason as a new metric (sre.kv.evictions; labels: model_family, reason); create threshold alert when eviction_rate > 5% over 5m.
- Circuit-breaker: implement a protection layer to return 429 early for sessions hitting >X cache misses in Y window to stop regen thundering.
- Alerts: convert exporter restart alert to a flapped-alert that requires 3 restarts in 10m to fire (reduce noise).

Runbook checklist for handoff (to be pasted in Zoom/Slack)
- Today’s active cards: paste xIDs (use short title)
- Any ongoing mitigation toggles: yes/no + which (e.g., cache TTL increased to 90s)
- Escalation path: Pager -> SRE lead -> Platform eng -> Model infra on-call (if model-level kernel regressions observed)
- Known flaky dashboards: "generation/kv-hit" flagged as noisy (ignore single-point blips under 10s)

Open questions for follow-up
- Do we want a dedicated burst pool for large enterprise evals or better QoS shaping at the LB? Tradeoffs: cost vs isolation.
- What’s the acceptable default cache TTL for session KV given the new prompt behaviors from customers? (30s -> 90s working but needs AB test)
- Can we detect "eval-like" traffic patterns at the gateway to label requests and route to a different autoscaler profile?

Action items (assignments)
- Carlos: add zone-aware autoscaler logging + small PR to add cooldown (infra#4821). ETA 2027-06-09.
- Priya: instrument kv.evictions metric and create dashboard; add 5% eviction alert. ETA 2027-06-08.
- Leah: run canary for bursty batched requests (canary/burst-0627) and produce short report. ETA 2027-06-07.
- SRE rotation: reduce exporter liveness sensitivity in next deploy (ops-pr-4890). ETA: included in next patch.

Notes-to-self / misc (scrappy bits we had in chat)
- When documenting the autoscaler fix, include the exact spike trace and the org-id (redacted) that created the burst; this makes future debugging fast.
- Short-term config toggles (cache TTL bump) are OK but add a quick backout plan: revert TTL and flush session store if we see regen cascade.

Meeting follow-ups
- Agenda item for next SRE sync (2027-06-09): present results of the KV eviction metric and canary outcome; decide on permanent cache TTL and autoscaler cooldown policy.
- Invitees: SRE rotation, infra-autoscale owners, model-ops rep.

Appendix: useful links and quick commands
- Canary runbook: confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Canary+Procedures
- Quick triage script: ssh ops@runner && /opt/sre/scripts/triage.sh --since 10m --labels generation
- Grafana dashboards: dashboards/generation/kv-hit / dashboards/autoscaler/zone-balance

If you skim only one thing: keep the Handoff Signal Card format in your mental pocket. During the handoff, paste the card into the Slack channel and ask the incoming oncall to "ack + 1 action" (acknowledge and call out one immediate follow-up). That simple ritual reduces half of the context loss we see in cross-shift disputes.
